derivation.graph_laplacian: L = D - W with W_ij = exp(-|x_i-x_j|^2 / epsilon_k) on the cutoff stencil
derivation.induced_operator: Lhat_h = -(2 / (mu_2 h^2)) L, with mu_2 the discrete second moment of the kernel stencil
derivation.target: Lhat_h f -> Delta f on interior nodes as h -> 0

baseline_cubic_interior.observation: the kernel-induced graph operator reproduces the quadratic test exactly and converges toward the continuum Laplacian on the cubic interior scan
baseline_cubic_interior.conclusion: after discrete second-moment normalization, the cubic baseline remains a clean scalar continuum control; broader kernels remain less accurate at finite resolution

derivation.local_operator: fit a quadratic Taylor polynomial around each point with the same kernel weights and read off the Laplacian from the quadratic coefficients
derivation.target: the kernel-weighted local recovery remains convergent on weakly jittered point sets after excluding a boundary buffer matched to the kernel radius

point_set_control.observation: the weakly perturbed point-set scan only partially preserves scalar convergence
point_set_control.conclusion: mild geometric disorder still distorts the current operator recovery enough that CP1 is not yet closed on point-set controls

derivation.boundary_extension: extend the same stencil by homogeneous reflected ghost values; odd parity for Dirichlet and even parity for Neumann
derivation.target: the induced operator remains convergent on full-domain boundary-compatible test families

boundary_controls.observation: reflected boundary controls retain convergence on both Dirichlet and Neumann-compatible test families
boundary_controls.conclusion: the same local kernel regime remains stable when the cubic scan is extended from interior-only error to explicit homogeneous boundary-control families

observation: the scalar operator retains some continuum structure, but at least one CP1 control family is still unstable
conclusion: CP1 is only partially closed: the cubic baseline remains informative, but point-set or boundary-control robustness still needs more work
